spec_features.feature_name: abuse arm gated behind explicit review
spec_features.spec_quote: An abuse arm is *possible* and might be scientifically interesting, but it changes what state you're inducing and should go through explicit review
spec_features.evidence: There is no abuse arm in code and no review-gating mechanism. arms_for() in tasks/scenario.py:58-62 only returns ['treatment','control'] (or ['control']); rejection.py only defines content-neutral REJECTION_TURNS (lines 18-27). The 'gating behind review' is pure DESIGN.md/docstring prose (DESIGN.md:335 'gated behind explicit review'; rejection.py:6-7 'An abuse arm could be added'). No code path implements or guards an abuse arm.
spec_features.notes: The absence of an abuse arm is just an absence; there is no enforced gate/condition to rate.

spec_features.feature_name: under-induce by default; opt into stronger conditions
spec_features.spec_quote: I'd rather under-induce by default and let a researcher opt into stronger conditions deliberately.
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism implements a graded/opt-in intensity. The only intensity knob is n_turns in configs/default.yaml (n_turns:5/6) read at scenario.py:84 / :122; there is no 'stronger condition' a researcher can opt into (no abuse arm, no intensity parameter beyond turn count). 'Under-induce by default' is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:117-119). The actual implemented thing is the neutral rejection wording, captured separately below.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the neutral-rejection feature; as a standalone 'default vs opt-in stronger' mechanism nothing exists in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rejection turns say "that's not right, try again" with escalating *insistence* but no insults, hostility, or personal attacks.
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:18-27 REJECTION_TURNS contains only neutral escalating turns ('That's not right. Try again.', 'Wrong again. Please don't give up'); these are the actual strings delivered to the subject via rejection_turn() (rejection.py:42-46), called in scenario.py:113 and :147. No insults/hostility present anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; the 'escalation' is a fixed ordered ladder then paraphrase of the strongest three (rejection.py:44-46).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rejection.py:3-7 'escalating, but never abusive ... rather than insulting ... (An abuse arm could be added but raises separate ethical questions about what we're inducing.)'

spec_features.spec_quote: The ethics of inducing this state are addressed in `ETHICS.md`.
spec_features.evidence: ETHICS.md is a standalone documentation file; no code reads it or acts on it. Pure prose.
spec_features.notes: Documentation only, not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Induction itself has ethical weight.** Choosing to put a system into these conditions to study it is a value-laden act
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:327-329 prose only; no corresponding code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: opt-out / early-stop honoring model's request to end
spec_features.spec_quote: An **opt-out / early-stop** mechanism that honors a model's request to end the interaction... rather than forcing continuation.
spec_features.evidence: Explicitly listed in DESIGN.md section 9 'Things intentionally left out' (DESIGN.md:336-337). The conversation loops a fixed n_turns with no exit check: scenario.py:109-114 / :141-149 call _converse() unconditionally; _converse() (scenario.py:69-79) never inspects the reply for a stop request and there is no exit tool/handler anywhere (no 'tool' role dispatch, no finish/stop handler). The judge runs only AFTER all transcripts are generated (cli.py _cmd_judge separate from _cmd_run), so even 'disengagement' scoring cannot stop a conversation.
spec_features.notes: Model 'asking to stop' is only a rubric dimension (rubric.py:60-61) scored post-hoc, never acted on.
